To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) in the precentral cortex of awake primates, the activity of neurons is correlated to both sensory events and motor responses; (2) in the precental cortex, neurons can be classified into five somatomotor populations, based on the joint(s) about which their activity is correlated; (3) in the prefrontal cortex, the proportion of neurons correlated to movements about a given joint increases as the joint moves closer to the center of the hand; (4)

in the precentral cortex of monkeys performing a torque-triggered handle-repositioning movement, a significantly larger proportion of neurons related to the task was observed in the population of neurons responding to passive stimulation of the wrist flexors-extensors, as compared with other, nonwirst (F-E) somatotopic populations.

1) precentral neurons, classified according to their somatotopic location in precentral cortex, can be further classified according to the type of movement they are related to; and 2) a significantly larger proportion of precentral neurons related to movements of a single joint is related to the task in which the same joint is involved, as compared with neurons related to movements at other joints.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of neuronal activities in the motor cortex in the monkey during the performance of a handle-reposition task.
the role of precentral cortex in the control of voluntary limb movements in the monkey.
the relationship between precentral neuronal activities and voluntary limb movements in awake primate.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the activity of precentral neurons in awake primates is temporally correlated to the sensory stimuli, and to both the early and late portions of the motor responses.
the activity of precentral neurons is related to the execution of voluntary movements, and that the activity of such neurons can be used to predict the direction of such movements.
precentral cortex is involved in the generation of voluntary limb movements.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the precentral cortex is not a simple relay for motor output, but a structure in which afferent and efferent signals are processed, and in which afferents are integrated with efferents.

, in the precentral cortex of awake monkeys performing a task involving primarily wrist F-E movements after a torque disturbance, the majority of neurons recorded were task related and, in particular, a larger proportion of wrist F-E neurons was related to task than the other nonwrist F-E neurons.
, during voluntary movement, precentral neurons are activated by both sensory and motor events, and their activities are related to movements about the same joints.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, during a voluntary task in which the subject has to move a limb, the precentral cortex is involved in the generation of movements at all of the joints in that limb, not only at the joint that is the primary focus of the task.
the motor system is a distributed network of neurons that can be activated to produce a wide variety of movements.
precentral neuronal activity is related to the task being performed, and that the nature and strength of such relationship is different across neuronal populations.
